::: {#def-chi-square-test}
#### Pearson's chi-square test of independence

With observed counts $O_{ij}$ and [expected counts](#def-expected-count) $E_{ij}$
in an $r \times c$ contingency table,
**Pearson's chi-square test** of the null hypothesis
that the row and column variables are independent
uses the statistic

$$X^2 \eqdef \sumto{i}{r} \sumto{j}{c} \frac{(O_{ij} - E_{ij})^2}{E_{ij}}.$$

Its p-value is $\Pr(W \ge X^2)$,
where $W$ has the $\chi^2_{(r-1)(c-1)}$ distribution
([chi-square distribution](inference.qmd#def-chi-square-dist)).
:::
